Sky News politics live blog — entry timestamped Thu 24 September 2026 01:00 BST; page updated 07:39 BST Thu 24 Sep

HEADLINE: Exclusive mega poll reveals Burnham bounce, a problem for Farage, and a hung parliament on the horizon
(Exclusive YouGov MRP poll for Sky News and The Times)

FACTS (Sky News's own wording):
- "Labour would win the most seats in an election tomorrow, according to the first YouGov-Sky-Times MRP polling projection in a year."
- "The party is back in first place after Reform UK went from pole position to third, in a projection that puts Britain on course for a hung parliament with no party securing an overall majority."
- "Labour would need the help of more than one other party to secure a statistical majority in the House of Commons since it falls far short." / "at least two other parties".
- "The scale of political change in this parliament, with the collapse and partial repair of Labour and the rise and fall of Reform, has been dramatic."
- On Labour seats won at the 2024 election: "It shows how many of them were projected to turn into Reform seats in YouGov's polling this time last year. However, with Burnham now as prime minister, it reveals that Labour would win back around half those seats back in this latest MRP projection."
- "The total sample size for the poll was 14,000 people, and the fieldwork was carried out between 23 August and 18 September."
- Presented by Sky deputy political editor Sam Coates.

NOTE: Exact seat totals were shown only in an embedded Flourish Sankey chart and a video, not in scraped article text. DO NOT quote specific seat numbers from this cache file. Verified qualitative findings only.

--- OTHER ENTRIES FROM THE SAME LIVE BLOG ---

19:45 BST Wed 23 Sep — Sir Tony Blair calls for UK to 'rejoin the EU within a decade'
TBI report: "Britain should play a leading role in shaping a more powerful Europe. The necessary reforms have already been identified – not least in Mario Draghi's report on EU competitiveness – but implementing them remains the challenge. For Britain to be part of that effort, it must show political commitment to Europe. This can be achieved by setting a clear, public objective to rejoin the EU within a decade – subject to internal EU reform. This objective should be a cornerstone of the UK government's upcoming 10-year plan."
QUOTE — TONY BLAIR (foreword): "There is no point in inching towards Europe as we feel what British public opinion might accommodate. We should be clear that we want back into a formal relationship with the EU. But it must be a Europe on a credible path to reform, a Europe of nation states, a Europe capable of being a genuine global power."
Blair noted the EU inviting Canada to become its first associate member showed a "newfound flexibility".

18:55 BST Wed 23 Sep — Benefit claimants could be banned from buying alcohol and cigarettes under Tory plans
QUOTE — KEMI BADENOCH: "If you can work, you should work. Helping people into work is not punishment. The best welfare is a well-paid job. So, we will be tough on those who exploit the system because the current system is unfair to workers, taxpayers and those who truly need support. We should not be borrowing from our children and grandchildren to support people who simply refuse to work. Welfare must be a safety net for those who genuinely need it, not a lifestyle choice for those who can't be bothered."
- Every two years a UC claimant has worked qualifies them for an extra year on the full rate. Reduced rate worth 70p for every pound of the full rate. Pre-payment card can buy food, everyday essentials and pay bills.
- Conservatives estimate £538m a year saved, 350,000 claimants moved to a new "subsistence allowance".
- Robert Jenrick, Reform UK's Treasury spokesman, described it as "a sticking plaster on a wound they opened". A Labour spokesperson said the measures were "unworkable".

17:15 BST Wed 23 Sep — Burnham: We'll be 'conscious' of Starmer and Reeves's tax rises in budget
QUOTE — ANDY BURNHAM (to journalists, asked if the balance between tax and spend was right): "We have two budgets in 2024 and 2025 and we have to be conscious of the extent to which we have raised revenue. And we have to make sure we get the balance right." Pushed on whether the balance was right, he said the matter was one for the budget.

17:00 BST Wed 23 Sep — Drinking ban at football matches could be scrapped, says Burnham
QUOTE — ANDY BURNHAM (speaking on his UN trip in New York): "I don't think it's fair for football fans to be singled out in that way and I made that point. I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different, and I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination. There are different ways it could be done - it could happen on a trial basis. But I'm not going to back away from what's been a long held view of mine. I don't see how it can be fair that some supporters of one sport can be treated differently."
(Drinking in football stands was made illegal in 1985 over hooliganism concerns.)
The UK Football Policing Unit said it would like to meet the PM to "discuss his views and explain the challenges these proposed changes would bring to policing and the safety of staff and fans at football games", adding: "Other sports simply don't see the violence and criminal behaviour from their supporters that football does, albeit a minority, with alcohol often playing a significant part in violent and disorderly behaviour. It would be irresponsible to fuel this by allowing greater alcohol consumption during games."
[NOTE: football-adjacent — Daily Brief has a no-sport rule; this is licensing legislation, use only if framed as a legal/policy change, or skip.]

14:43 BST Wed 23 Sep — Argentina not behaving like a democracy in Falklands row, says UK
Argentine President Javier Milei repeated Argentina's claim to the Falklands at the UN General Assembly and said the islanders do not have a right to self-determination, calling for negotiations with the UK.
UK delegation to the UN statement (posted @UKUN_NewYork 17:54 BST 23 Sep): "The United Kingdom has no doubt about its sovereignty over the Falkland Islands." And: "Argentina continues to deny that this fundamental human right applies to the people of the Falkland Islands, and actively seeks opportunities in international fora to assert its sovereignty claim. This behaviour is wholly incompatible with the principles established in the United Nations charter and is not the behaviour we expect of a democracy."
